text: I step over to the tavern runner and hold out a coin. "Stew later. What's the rumor worth paying for, and does it have anything to do with that missing patrol on the board?"
motivation: A tavern runner is selling news for a coin while the notice board warns about a missing patrol.
intended: I want the local rumor and whether it connects to the missing patrol.

text: I keep my voice low and don't take the coin back yet. "Who saw those footprints, and how long ago? Did anyone from the gate actually go look, or is this just travelers talking?"
motivation: The runner just tied the missing patrol to muddy footprints northwest of the crates and said that spot is worth watching.
intended: I want to know how fresh and reliable the footprint rumor is before I act on it.

text: I turn to the guard captain and keep my voice down. "If the timing matches their last check-in, why hasn't the watch gone to look? What was that patrol supposed to be doing when they vanished?"
motivation: The captain just confirmed no one from the gate has inspected the morning footprints by the northwest crates.
intended: I want the watch's reason for waiting and what the missing patrol was last assigned to do.

text: I glance toward the crowded gate, then back at the captain. "Whose orders are you waiting on, and do you think they want this left alone? If I'm walking out to that milestone, I want to know what I'm walking into."
motivation: The captain says higher-up orders have held back a search, and travelers last saw the patrol heading toward an old milestone northwest.
intended: I want to know who is delaying the search and whether the milestone lead is safe to follow.

text: I lean in, matching the captain's low voice. "Hornet's nest — whose? What are the brass afraid of finding if someone actually goes and looks?"
motivation: The captain says the city watch commander has given no order, and the brass seem afraid of stirring a hornet's nest.
intended: I want to know what the commanders fear is out by that milestone.

text: I hold the captain's look and keep my voice just as low. "Old secrets and unsettled scores — whose? If the brass won't name them, who around this gate still will?"
motivation: The captain says the trouble past the northwest milestone is old secrets and unsettled scores that higher command wants left buried.
intended: I want a name or a person who will say whose quarrel is waiting out there.

text: I give the captain a small nod and step back to the tavern runner, keeping my voice under the rain. "The captain says the gate won't talk. You will. Whose debts and noble quarrels sit past that milestone, and what does a loose tongue cost around here?"
motivation: The captain says the brass have sealed every mouth at the gate and names the tavern runner as someone who might still know more.
intended: I want the runner to name whose debts and intrigues are tied to the missing patrol.

text: I slide another coin toward him, slower this time. "Then sell me one name. Which family, and what debt would make a patrol vanish before their next report?"
motivation: The runner says noble family debts sit past the milestone, and that a thicker purse is what buys a careful answer.
intended: I want one family name and the debt that could explain the missing patrol.

text: I leave the coin where it is and follow his glance around the square. "Then point. Who here has those deeper roots, and will they talk to a stranger with a thin purse?"
motivation: The runner says the scores are too tangled for him to name, and that I need someone with deeper roots than his.
intended: I want him to point me at a person in this square who will actually name names.

text: I tilt my head toward the quieter fringe of the square, away from the guards. "Then not here. Walk with me as far as the notice board, and tell me who you meant."
motivation: The ragged stranger just refused to name anyone while we are still standing in the open square.
intended: I want them to step aside with me and say who has the deeper roots.
